For each survey report reviewed, the purpose was to identify the main objective of the research, the research methodology, the survey participants, the study findings, and whether contractor perspectives and decision-making regarding training and hiring were considered. A total of 17 reports were reviewed, five of which were highly relevant to this study; these are shown in Table 1. Surveys commonly focused on profiling contractors and exploring challenges with the labor market and technologies and the types of training contractors partake in. Some surveys asked about contractors’ familiarity with rebates for building upgrades and their expectations for installation increases in the coming years; however, there was a lack of further inquiry into the implications of these findings for hiring and training decisions. There was a gap in exploring which factors influence contractors’ decisions to hire new employees or upskill their existing workforce—this includes a limited assessment of what kind of information and messaging from other stakeholders in the market influence contractor behavior. This study addresses that gap by directly examining when and why contractors choose to hire and train other contractors. 3 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
